creator: Dan McCreary

Learning graph
Generative AI

dublinCore.description: Interactive infographic of the workflow for building an intelligent textbook: a course description leads through Bloom's taxonomy, concept enumeration and concept dependencies to a learning graph, which feeds book-level outputs and chapter-level content.
relation: About the Signal Processing with AI Website

learningObjectives: Trace the primary path in row one from the Course Description to the Learning Graph, naming the five boxes in order and the side branch through Concept Taxonomy
Explain why the Learning Graph is the central step: it is the only box with arrows into all five book-level outputs, and ten components lie downstream of it
Distinguish book-level outputs (row two, light blue) from chapter-level content (row three, light green) and name the box the chapter-level items depend on
Predict how many components are downstream of a chosen box, then verify the count with the hover highlight
Identify the boxes that have nothing downstream and say what they have in common
prerequisites: A general idea of a course description and learning objectives

misconceptions.misconception: The workflow is one straight line from the course description to the finished book
misconceptions.correction: Only row one is a chain, and it branches at Concept Enumeration; the Learning Graph then fans out to five book-level outputs
misconceptions.evidence: Hover over Concept Enumeration: 13 boxes are highlighted as downstream

misconceptions.misconception: Every output is generated directly from the Learning Graph
misconceptions.correction: The chapter-level items depend on Chapters & Sections, not directly on the Learning Graph
misconceptions.evidence: The arrows into row three start at Chapters & Sections, and hovering Glossary of Terms highlights none of the row-three boxes

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Workflow diagram for generating an intelligent textbook. A Course Description leads through the 2001 Bloom Taxonomy, Concept Enumeration and Concept Dependencies to the Learning Graph, with Concept Taxonomy as a side branch. The Learning Graph feeds five book-level outputs; Chapters and Sections feeds five chapter-level items.

responsiveBreakpoints.description: Below about 600 px the box labels shrink from 16 px toward 12 px and the first row uses taller boxes
Below about 500 px long words in the box labels are hyphenated
Phone width: 12 px box labels and a two-line footer in the description panel

visualElements.description: Sixteen boxes in three rows joined by sixteen arrows: the path to the Learning Graph, five book-level outputs and five chapter-level items
Panel with the hovered component's name, level, description and count of downstream components
Legend of the stage, book-level and chapter-level colors

model.description: A directed graph of 16 components. Hovering a component highlights every component reachable from it by following arrows (its downstream set) and reports the size of that set
algorithms: Depth-first reachability over the arrow list

instructionalStrategies: Follow the arrows from the Course Description to the outputs
extensions: Open each box's documentation page and compare its inputs with the arrows into that box
